entries.title: NBER working papers are recognised as papers
entries.body: Paste a link to an NBER working paper (its page, its PDF or its DOI link) and the app fetches the paper's PDF. A link that is followed successfully and ends at the address of a paper source the app already recognises is also treated as a paper, not an ordinary web page. Some papers may still not be retrievable.

entries.title: Pasting a paper's link again finds the paper
entries.body: The app keeps the address you pasted, even when the paper itself lives at a different one. Paste the same link again and it finds the paper you already have instead of importing it a second time. This applies to papers added from this version on, not to older ones. The pasted address is also kept in an article's export.

entries.title: The "wider window" notice goes away
entries.body: In a window too narrow to show notes beside the article, the line saying "The notes need a wider window" sat over the foot of the text with no way to remove it. It fades out by itself after a few seconds, unless your mouse is over it, and has a close button that dismisses it at once.

entries.title: Chat buttons show a chat icon
entries.body: The button for asking about a paragraph, the headers of the chat windows, and the marks showing an existing conversation in Glossary, Citations and Debate use a pair of speech bubbles in place of a single one. The single bubble is the icon for comments, so the chat button could be mistaken for a comment.

entries.title: A single comment shows its words once
entries.body: When a passage had one comment beside it, opening that comment repeated its words. The words now appear once: a comment with no answer opens and closes within its own line, and an AI answer opens beneath the comment without repeating it. Closed notes no longer leave an empty gap either.
